            color = grid[r][c]

            while c2 + 1 < cmax and grid[r][c2+1] == color:

def find_all_rectangular_regions(grid, rows, cols):
    regions = []
    visited = set()
    
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if (r,c) in visited:
                continue
            color = grid[r][c]
            
            c1, c2 = c, c
            while c2 + 1 < cols and grid[r][c2+1] == color:
                c2 += 1
            
            r1, r2 = r, r
            while r2 + 1 < rows:
                all_same = all(grid[r2+1][cc] == color for cc in range(c1, c2+1))

# Check ALL maximal regions in input grid to understand the full pattern

def find_all_maximal_regions(grid):
    regions = []
    visited = set()
    
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if (r,c) in visited:
                continue
            color = grid[r][c]
            
            c1, c2 = c, c
            while c2 + 1 < cols and grid[r][c2+1] == color:
                c2 += 1
            
            r1, r2 = r, r
            while r2 + 1 < rows:
                all_same = all(grid[r2+1][cc] == color for cc in range(c1, c2+1))
                if all_same:
                    r2 += 1
                else:
                    break
            
            region_cells = set((rr, cc) for rr in range(r1, r2+1) for cc in range(c1, c2+1))
            new_cells = region_cells - visited
            if new_cells:
                regions.append((r1, r2, c1, c2, color, len(new_cells)))
                visited.update(region_cells)
    
    return regions
